title: Same-document replacements do not preserve the navigation API key

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

For the following following test (found when debugging a crash on a live site, this is one of the issues reduced from that)

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<script src="/resources/testharness.js"></script>
<script src="/resources/testharnessreport.js"></script>
<script>
test(() => {
  const key = navigation.currentEntry.key;
  history.replaceState(null, "", "?replaced");
  assert_equals(navigation.currentEntry.key, key);
}, "history.replaceState() preserves the navigation API key");
</script>
```


(already tested in [WPT](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/navigation-api/navigation-history-entry/current-basic.html), but fully reduced)


In the [URL and history update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#url-and-history-update-steps),

- For step 2. activeEntry = navigable's active session history entry with a key of K0
- Step 3. newEntry = a new session history entry which gets a fresh key K1 (new UUID)
- Step 5.  entryToReplace set to activeEntry
- Step 10. navigable's active session history entry is step to newEntry
- Step 11. Update the navigation API entries for a same-document navigation given navigation, newEntry, "replace"

In [update the navigation API for a same document navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-the-navigation-api-entries-for-a-same-document-navigation)

- Step 6 disposes of oldCurrentNHE (newEntry)
- Step 7 creates a new NavigationHistoryEntry with newEntry, so navigation.currentEntry is newEntry with a fresh navigation API key (K1)


This means when we exit the URL and history update steps the following assertion fails:

`assert_equals(navigation.currentEntry.key, key);`

as the new key is a fresh UUID.
